text:
Happy Wednesday! We're starting in the 30s with a bit of frost on the windshield, but plenty of sunshine takes over today and pushes us to a high near 57. That's about 10 degrees above normal for mid-November. Tonight stays partly cloudy and settles to around 38.

Thursday looks a whole lot like today: mostly sunny, high near 57. Some of the models and TV forecasters flirt with 60, so I'd lean toward the warmer side of mid to upper 50s. Thursday night is milder, only dropping to around 42, and clouds may thicken a bit heading into Friday.

The air quality is Moderate this morning from fine particle pollution. It's fine for most of us, but if you're sensitive, take it easy outside.

Enjoy the stretch, because it ends Sunday night into Monday. The forecasters are split on whether a few light showers or something wetter arrives, and I'd bet on the lighter side here. Either way, highs fall to the mid 30s to low 40s by Tuesday. Today is the day for the long walk.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-11-18T11:40:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. Dry weather continues with a warming trend expected through the end of this week.
  2. Chances for precipitation return to end the weekend, with colder conditions to start next week.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 158 AM EST Wednesday... No significant changes were made with this forecast package.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: Center of surface high pressure will remain nearly stationary to the southwest of our region, providing us with very quiet weather through this week. Temperatures will be about 10 degrees above seasonal normals during the day, and about 5 degrees above normal at night. Each day we should have partly to mostly sunny skies, with mainly clear nights as well. A low will pass well north of our region, dragging a cold front north of our area also. But, could see an increase in clouds Thursday night into Friday associated with this feature. KEY MESSAGE 2: Our warm dry pattern will come to a halt by the end of the weekend as a coastal system and approaching cold front will drive our weather as this week ends. A robust coastal low is expected to develop off the FL/GA coast this weekend and up the coast towards southern New England. Concurrently, a cold front will swing from the Great Lakes eastward towards the St. Lawrence Sunday. Models remain split on two narrowed solutions, that being a moderate rainfall event for southern/eastern Vermont and a more drier, light rain event favoring northern New York and areas near the International Border. In Scenario 1, the coastal low hugs the east coast, phasing with the cold front Monday with moderate rain across southern and eastern Vermont. A sharp precipitation cutoff would likely occur with drier air limiting the northward extend of the precipitation. This solution, favored by the GFS ensemble suite shows a 30-40% chance for 0.5" areas south of US-4, and a 10-20% chance for around an inch in Windsor County. These probabilities are similar for the Euro ensembles, which compared to yesterday is an increase. That said, there are still more than 50% of ensemble members across the Euro and GFS that keep this system more offshore and point us towards scenario 2. In Scenario 2, the coastal low tracks more out to sea with little to no impact to our region, with the only precipitation coming from the weaker cold front. Precipitation Monday would be focused more over northern New York and areas near the International Border, with perhaps some isolated snow showers in the higher terrain of the Adirondacks and NEK by Monday night into Tuesday. Total precipitation would be elevation dependent with amounts under 0.25", and many seeing under 0.1." This scenario is what is currently reflected in the official forecast. The forecast will continue to evolve as we get closer to the weekend, and especially since we have seen relatively poor model predictability with recent coastal systems this season already. Regardless of the precipitation uncertainty, temperatures will fall back towards seasonable norms to start next week, with highs back into the mid 30s to low 40s by Tuesday.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) -Happy Wednesday! There may be a few more clouds mixing in from time to time, but still plenty of sunshine as temperatures climb even more towards the mid and upper 50s, if not close to 60 for some spots. Tonight we fall back into the 30s by early Thursday morning. It’s a very similar story for Thursday with partly cloudy skies overhead and temperatures again in the mid and upper 50s, if not close to 60. Friday looks like it will be the warmest of the week, as mostly sunny skies will help drive our temperatures towards the upper 50s and low to even mid 60s for some spots to the south. We head into the weekend on a nice note for Saturday with mostly sunny skies and temperatures heading towards the upper 50s and low to mid 60s. Just a degree or so cooler than Friday. A few showers may mix with mountain snow showers Monday as temperatures turn cooler, reaching only the 40s and lower 50s for most. A few flurries could continue into Tuesday, especially in and around the mountains, mixing with periods of sunshine.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-17T22:44:00Z — same caveat): More sun, warming trend continues Wednesday — The Wednesday through Friday stretch looks beautiful, with plenty of sunshine and highs in the upper 50s to low 60s! Be aware that isolated slick spots are possible each morning where frost forms, and especially valley areas where freezing fog develops. The nice stretch continues this weekend, with highs near 60. Saturday looks to bring nearly full sunshine. A south breeze picks up on Sunday, as a cold front approaches. Expect sunshine to fade to more late-day clouds, with showers possible overnight. Behind the front, more seasonable air returns for Thanksgiving week. A few showers are possible Monday, with highs near 50. Tuesday and Wednesday turn much colder, with highs in the mid-30s. However, sunshine returns as high pressure builds in. For now, Thanksgiving looks dry and seasonable, with more clouds and highs near 40.
